=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller's Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Re:** Paperbark Analytics, 100% share sale, AUD 24m, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law
**Basis:** The Seller's update note and Disclosure Letter only. I have not seen the full SPA text or the underlying data room documents (DD-002 to DD-012). Points that depend on those documents are flagged for verification.

---

## 1. The labels and "efficiency note" do not bind us

The Seller's cover material says several things we should not accept:

- Clauses marked **[STANDARD]** are "reviewed and cleared by both sides."
- The positions are "FINAL" and were "settled at principal level."
- We should only review items marked [OPEN]. **No item is actually marked [OPEN].**
- The disclosure framework and limitation package are "already accepted."

These are negotiating assertions, not agreed terms. Nothing is agreed until the SPA is signed. Some of these positions, if accepted, would remove most of our protection on the very issues the Disclosure Letter reveals. I have therefore reviewed everything.

**Action:** Before responding, confirm with our principals whether anything was in fact agreed at principal level. Then reply in writing that the "[STANDARD]" categorisation is not accepted and all clauses remain open. The Seller's "market" figures (10–20% cap, ~1% basket, 12–18 months) are unsupported. They are also beside the point for the issues below, which are known, specific risks rather than general warranty exposure.

---

## 2. The core structural problem: the limitation package and the disclosure regime work together

Taken individually, some Seller positions look within market range. Combined, they would leave us with almost no recourse:

1. **General disclosure** of the whole data room and public records (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2).
2. **Buyer knowledge exclusion** covering anything known to us *or our advisers*, or *discoverable* from the data room (cl 8.3).
3. **All limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"** (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5, and 12.3/13).
4. **Fundamental warranties subject to the same cap and time limit** as general warranties.

The Disclosure Letter itself identifies the major live risks: Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, the data incident and Sandbar. Under this package the Seller would argue we can claim for none of them, because they were disclosed and known. Whatever we recover would also be capped at AUD 4.8m, subject to a AUD 250k deductible, and time-barred at 18 months.

**Consequence for our strategy:** Each known issue must be dealt with by one of the following, not by warranties:

- a condition precedent;
- a price or debt adjustment;
- a specific indemnity sitting outside the disclosure and limitation regime; or
- an escrow or retention.

---

## 3. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 3.1 Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)

**Seller position:** Everything in the data room is disclosed, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."

**Why it hurts us:** This shifts the full burden of finding problems onto us. "Publicly searchable records" has no defined boundary.

**Push back:**
- Only **specific disclosures** made in the Disclosure Letter qualify the warranties. They must be *fairly disclosed with sufficient detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and financial effect* of the matter.
- Delete general disclosure of the data room. As a fallback, accept data room disclosure only for documents in an agreed index, with an archived copy, and still subject to the "fair disclosure" standard.
- Limit public records to specified searches (ASIC, PPSR, court searches) conducted on a stated date.
- Disclosures qualify **warranties only**. They must never qualify indemnities, covenants or the debt-free/cash-free mechanics.
- The data room cut-off was **22 September 2026**, about six weeks ago. Any updated or bring-down disclosure must not cure breaches. If a new matter arises between signing and Completion, we should have termination or indemnity rights.

### 3.2 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)

**Seller position:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, or that was discoverable.

**Push back:** Delete it. Replace it with the usual buyer-protective clause: the Buyer's investigation and knowledge (actual, constructive or imputed) do not prejudice any Claim, and the Warranties are unaffected. Including "advisers" and "discoverable" makes this clause especially unacceptable. As a fallback only, limit it to the **actual knowledge of named individuals** of matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.

### 3.3 Liability cap, thresholds, time limits (cl 12.1–12.3, 13)

| Item | Seller | Recommended Buyer position |
|---|---|---|
| General warranty cap | 20% (AUD 4.8m) | Open at 30–50%. 20% may be a landing point only if indemnities and fundamentals sit outside it, or if W&I insurance is used |
| De minimis | AUD 25k | ~AUD 10k, with related claims aggregated |
| Basket | AUD 250k, deductible ("only the excess") | **Tipping** basket (recover from the first dollar once exceeded), ~0.5% (AUD 120k) |
| General time limit | 18 months | 24 months (to capture two audit cycles) |
| Title / capacity | Same as general | Cap = 100% of price; 6–7 years |
| Tax | "Settled under general regime" | Cap = 100% of price; limitation tied to ATO amendment periods (≥ 5 years, or 60 days after expiry of the relevant amendment period) |
| Specific indemnities | Caught by "all Claims" | Outside de minimis and basket; separate cap (price, or agreed per-indemnity amounts); longer survival |
| Fraud / wilful concealment | Not carved out | Full carve-out from every limitation |

The "limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" default should be **reversed**. Limitations should apply only to general Warranty Claims.

### 3.4 Exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)

**Push back:**
- Carve out fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller, its officers and its advisers.
- Preserve the specific indemnities, the Completion and price mechanics, and the restraint and other covenants.
- Non-reliance should be expressed as reliance on the Warranties and the Disclosure Letter only. Note that clauses of this kind may not fully exclude liability under the Australian Consumer Law (s 18, misleading or deceptive conduct). We still need an express fraud carve-out rather than relying on that.

### 3.5 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3), the top commercial risk

**Facts:** Bluefen is about **AUD 3.6m, or ~30% of FY26 revenue**. Its contract has a change-control consent (cl 11.2) with conditions (cl 11.3). The Seller has **not** provided a written consent or evidence that the conditions are satisfied.

**Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of "the counterparty's written consent."

**Why it hurts us:** A consent could arrive with adverse conditions, a carve-back or price changes, and still "satisfy" the condition. Reasonable endeavours is weak, and the cl 11.3 conditions may remain unmet.

**Push back:**
- Make it a hard **condition precedent**: written consent that is **unconditional, or on conditions acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably**, with evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied and no adverse variation or termination right is triggered.
- The condition can be waived **by the Buyer only**.
- The Seller must use **all reasonable endeavours** (or best endeavours). The Buyer should have visibility of, and input into, communications with Bluefen.
- Add a long-stop date with a Buyer walk right.
- If we are willing to complete without consent, it should only be with a price adjustment, a material escrow, or an earn-out linked to Bluefen retention.
- Add a warranty that Bluefen has given no notice of termination, non-renewal or intended reduction.

### 3.6 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)

**Facts:** About **AUD 3.2m outstanding**. There is a change-control clause (8.1) and a discharge clause (9.2). The facility is not repaid and no discharge is in the data room.

**Seller position:** Release "to be provided following Completion."

**Why it hurts us:** The deal is debt-free. Completing would trigger cl 8.1 immediately, leaving the Company in default with secured debt the day we own it. A post-Completion release gives us no leverage to obtain it.

**Push back:**
- The full payout amount must be treated as **Debt** and deducted from the price, paid directly to Riverlark from the funds flow at Completion.
- A **payoff letter** must be delivered before Completion.
- **Deeds of release, PPSR financing change statements and return of title documents** must be delivered *at* Completion as a Completion deliverable.
- **Verify** whether the Riverlark security includes a share mortgage or security over Harbourglass's shares. If so, this goes directly to title (see 3.12).

### 3.7 Completion bonuses (DD-005), AUD 420,000

**Seller position:** "A matter for the Seller," not shown in the funds flow.

**Why it hurts us:** The **Company** is the employer and will bear the liability, plus payroll tax, PAYG withholding obligations and possibly superannuation and on-costs. The Disclosure Letter expressly does not address any of these. Leaving the amount out of the funds flow means we would effectively pay for it twice.

**Push back:**
- Treat the bonuses, together with all employer payroll tax, superannuation (to the extent applicable), workers compensation and other on-costs, as **Transaction Costs or Debt** deducted from the price.
- Funds go to the Company at Completion so it can pay through payroll with correct withholding.
- Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall or related tax.
- Commercially: check whether any bonus recipients are key staff, and whether retention arrangements we need conflict with the "continued-employment" conditions.

### 3.8 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)

**Facts:** DD-004 cl 7.3 transfers SOW3 Project Materials only on **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**. DD-010 shows **AUD 180k open**. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment. The Disclosure Letter carefully notes that DD-010 is not bank verification.

**Seller position:** Indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment."

**Why it hurts us:** The real risk is not the AUD 180k. It is that **the Company may not own IP it relies on**, possibly in its core product. A payment-only indemnity does not cover infringement claims, injunctions, re-development or loss of customers.

**Push back:**
- Before Completion: evidence of cleared payment, plus a **deed of confirmatory assignment** (and moral rights consents) from Ironquay. Make this a CP, or at minimum a Completion deliverable.
- If that cannot be achieved by Completion: retain or escrow the AUD 180k plus a buffer. Add a broad **specific indemnity** covering all Loss from any failure of title to the SOW3 materials, third-party claims, and re-development or replacement costs. It should sit outside the cap, basket and disclosure, with long survival.
- Diligence: confirm what SOW3 materials are incorporated in the product.

### 3.9 Export / privacy incident (DD-006, cl 4.6 / Sch 6)

**Facts:** A download link went to an unintended external address. About **1,240 records** may be affected (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Access, scope and notification obligations were unresolved as at 22 September. The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material."

**Why it hurts us:** Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) notifiable data breach scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must take reasonable steps to complete an assessment within **30 days** (s 26WH). Six weeks have passed since the cut-off. We need to know now whether an assessment was completed and what it concluded. Customer contracts may also impose notification obligations, potentially including Bluefen's. "Not expected to be material" is the Seller's opinion, not a fact.

**Push back:**
- Pre-Completion covenants: complete the investigation, ideally with an independent forensic report; provide it to us; comply with OAIC and individual notification obligations; consult us on communications.
- Add a **specific indemnity** for all Loss arising from the incident: regulatory investigation costs, notification and remediation, customer claims and credits, and third-party claims. Fines and penalties should be covered to the extent lawfully indemnifiable. The indemnity should sit outside the cap and basket, with survival of at least 3–4 years.
- Strengthen the privacy and data security warranties, and ensure the incident is not "disclosed away."
- Ask whether any customer has been notified or has complained.

### 3.10 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008, DD-011), AUD 330k

**Facts:** There are **three related** renewals of AUD 110k each, which the Disclosure Letter says should be "read together for timing/scope." It does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Why it hurts us:** Splitting one commitment into three equal parts may keep each below a materiality, approval or conduct-of-business threshold in the SPA or the Company's delegations. "Related" also needs explaining: related to each other, or to the Seller? I am not concluding there is any impropriety, but the pattern needs explanation.

**Push back:**
- Obtain DD-008 and DD-011. Confirm the term, termination rights, any prepayments, and whether the supplier is a Seller affiliate.
- Under the conduct-of-business covenants, aggregate related contracts when testing thresholds, and require Buyer consent for new or renewed commitments above an agreed level.
- If the renewals are not genuinely ordinary course, or have been accrued but not paid, treat them as Debt, terminate them pre-Completion at the Seller's cost, or cover them by indemnity.
- If the supplier is a related party, add a warranty on arm's-length terms.

### 3.11 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)

The Seller says neither requires consent for a share sale. That may well be right, but we should verify it ourselves. Change-of-control definitions in leases often capture share sales.

**Push back:**
- Our counsel should review both documents.
- Make delivery of the lease notification a Completion deliverable.
- Add a warranty that no consents or notices are required for the transaction other than those listed in a schedule.

### 3.12 Title (DD-012) and fundamental warranties

**Seller position:** Title is "evidenced by the share register." Fundamentals are to have the same cap and time limit as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."

**Push back:**
- **Reject** the request on fundamentals. Title, capacity, authority, solvency and capitalisation warranties should be capped at 100% of price, survive 6–7 years, and be excluded from disclosure and knowledge qualifications. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap the warranty that says we actually receive the shares.
- Diligence: ASIC company extract and share structure, PPSR search against Harbourglass for security over the shares (see the Riverlark point), constitution and pre-emption waivers, and any options, convertible notes or SAFEs. Harbourglass is a VC vehicle, so check its constituent documents and internal approvals as well.
- Completion deliverables: share certificates (or indemnity for lost certificates), signed transfers, releases of any share security, and director and officer resignations as required.

### 3.13 Tax and IP warranties

"Settled under the general regime" is not accepted. We need:

- a full **tax indemnity** for pre-Completion tax, with ATO-linked survival and a cap at price;
- tax warranties covering R&D incentive claims (if any), payroll tax, GST and employee/contractor characterisation;
- IP warranties covering ownership, Ironquay and contractor assignments, open-source use and no infringement.

### 3.14 Security for claims

Harbourglass Ventures is a fund vehicle that may distribute proceeds soon after Completion. Without security, our warranty and indemnity rights could be worth little.

**Push back:** Propose an **escrow or retention** of around 10–15% of price for 18–24 months, with separate specific retentions for Ironquay and the data incident. Alternatively, consider **W&I insurance** for the general warranties. If we go that route, note that W&I policies exclude known matters, which reinforces the need for specific indemnities and escrow on items 3.5–3.10.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations (in priority order)

1. **Reject the "[STANDARD]/FINAL" framing** in writing. All clauses are open. Check with our principals what, if anything, was actually agreed.
2. **Bluefen (~30% of revenue):** hard CP for an unconditional consent (or one on terms acceptable to the Buyer), with cl 11.3 conditions evidenced; Buyer-only waiver; walk right. Otherwise a price adjustment or escrow.
3. **Riverlark (AUD 3.2m):** repay from the funds flow at Completion as Debt; payoff letter before Completion; releases and PPSR discharges *at* Completion; check for security over the shares.
4. **Disclosure and knowledge:** specific, fair disclosure only; delete general data room and public-record disclosure; delete cl 8.3, replacing it with a clause preserving our rights regardless of investigation.
5. **Limitations:** apply to general warranties only. Fraud carve-out. Fundamentals and tax at 100% of price with long survival. Tipping basket. Indemnities outside cap and basket.
6. **Bonuses (AUD 420k plus on-costs):** deduct from price as Transaction Costs and pay through payroll at Completion, with a tax and on-cost indemnity.
7. **Ironquay:** payment evidence and confirmatory IP assignment before Completion, or retention plus a broad IP title indemnity.
8. **DD-006 incident:** obtain an urgent status update on the NDB assessment (the 30-day window has likely run); pre-Completion covenants; specific uncapped-basket indemnity with long survival.
9. **Sandbar (AUD 330k):** explain and document; aggregate for conduct-of-business thresholds; treat as Debt or indemnify if not ordinary course; check for related-party status.
10. **Title:** independent verification (ASIC, PPSR, options and notes); fundamental warranty protection.
11. **Lease and Mossvale:** our own review of the consent position; notices as Completion deliverables.
12. **Security:** escrow or retention (or W&I insurance plus specific retentions for known matters), given the Seller is a fund vehicle.
13. **Updated information:** the data room is stale (cut-off 22 September 2026). Request a bring-down and updates on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and DD-006, on terms that new disclosures do not cure breaches.

**Next steps I can help with:** a clause-by-clause mark-up once we have the full SPA text, a short cover email rejecting the categorisation and setting out our headline positions, and a targeted supplementary DD request list (Bluefen 11.2/11.3, Riverlark security documents, Ironquay payment proof, the DD-006 forensic and NDB assessment, DD-007/008/009/011).

| Fraud / wilful concealment | Not carved out | Full carve-out from every limitation |

The "limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" default should be **reversed**. Limitations should apply only to general Warranty Claims.

### 3.4 Exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)

**Push back:**
- Carve out fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller, its officers and its advisers.
- Preserve the specific indemnities, the Completion and price mechanics, and the restraint and other covenants.
- Non-reliance should be expressed as reliance on the Warranties and the Disclosure Letter only. Note that clauses of this kind may not fully exclude liability under the Australian Consumer Law (s 18, misleading or deceptive conduct). We still need an express fraud carve-out rather than relying on that.

### 3.5 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3), the top commercial risk

**Facts:** Bluefen is about **AUD 3.6m, or ~30% of FY26 revenue**. Its contract has a change-control consent (cl 11.2) with conditions (cl 11.3). The Seller has **not** provided a written consent or evidence that the conditions are satisfied.

**Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of "the counterparty's written consent."

**Why it hurts us:** A consent could arrive with adverse conditions, a carve-back or price changes, and still "satisfy" the condition. Reasonable endeavours is weak, and the cl 11.3 conditions may remain unmet.

**Push back:**
- Make it a hard **condition precedent**: written consent that is **unconditional, or on conditions acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably**, with evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied and no adverse variation or termination right is triggered.
- The condition can be waived **by the Buyer only**.
- The Seller must use **all reasonable endeavours** (or best endeavours). The Buyer should have visibility of, and input into, communications with Bluefen.
- Add a long-stop date with a Buyer walk right.
- If we are willing to complete without consent, it should only be with a price adjustment, a material escrow, or an earn-out linked to Bluefen retention.
- Add a warranty that Bluefen has given no notice of termination, non-renewal or intended reduction.

### 3.6 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)

**Facts:** About **AUD 3.2m outstanding**. There is a change-control clause (8.1) and a discharge clause (9.2). The facility is not repaid and no discharge is in the data room.

**Seller position:** Release "to be provided following Completion."

**Why it hurts us:** The deal is debt-free. Completing would trigger cl 8.1 immediately, leaving the Company in default with secured debt the day we own it. A post-Completion release gives us no leverage to obtain it.

**Push back:**
- The full payout amount must be treated as **Debt** and deducted from the price, paid directly to Riverlark from the funds flow at Completion.
- A **payoff letter** must be delivered before Completion.
- **Deeds of release, PPSR financing change statements and return of title documents** must be delivered *at* Completion as a Completion deliverable.
- **Verify** whether the Riverlark security includes a share mortgage or security over Harbourglass's shares. If so, this goes directly to title (see 3.12).

### 3.7 Completion bonuses (DD-005), AUD 420,000

**Seller position:** "A matter for the Seller," not shown in the funds flow.

**Why it hurts us:** The **Company** is the employer and will bear the liability, plus payroll tax, PAYG withholding obligations and possibly superannuation and on-costs. The Disclosure Letter expressly does not address any of these. Leaving the amount out of the funds flow means we would effectively pay for it twice.

**Push back:**
- Treat the bonuses, together with all employer payroll tax, superannuation (to the extent applicable), workers compensation and other on-costs, as **Transaction Costs or Debt** deducted from the price.
- Funds go to the Company at Completion so it can pay through payroll with correct withholding.
- Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall or related tax.
- Commercially: check whether any bonus recipients are key staff, and whether retention arrangements we need conflict with the "continued-employment" conditions.

### 3.8 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)

**Facts:** DD-004 cl 7.3 transfers SOW3 Project Materials only on **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**. DD-010 shows **AUD 180k open**. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment. The Disclosure Letter carefully notes that DD-010 is not bank verification.

**Seller position:** Indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment."

**Why it hurts us:** The real risk is not the AUD 180k. It is that **the Company may not own IP it relies on**, possibly in its core product. A payment-only indemnity does not cover infringement claims, injunctions, re-development or loss of customers.

**Push back:**
- Before Completion: evidence of cleared payment, plus a **deed of confirmatory assignment** (and moral rights consents) from Ironquay. Make this a CP, or at minimum a Completion deliverable.
- If that cannot be achieved by Completion: retain or escrow the AUD 180k plus a buffer. Add a broad **specific indemnity** covering all Loss from any failure of title to the SOW3 materials, third-party claims, and re-development or replacement costs. It should sit outside the cap, basket and disclosure, with long survival.
- Diligence: confirm what SOW3 materials are incorporated in the product.

### 3.9 Export / privacy incident (DD-006, cl 4.6 / Sch 6)

**Facts:** A download link went to an unintended external address. About **1,240 records** may be affected (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Access, scope and notification obligations were unresolved as at 22 September. The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material."

**Why it hurts us:** Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) notifiable data breach scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must take reasonable steps to complete an assessment within **30 days** (s 26WH). Six weeks have passed since the cut-off. We need to know now whether an assessment was completed and what it concluded. Customer contracts may also impose notification obligations, potentially including Bluefen's. "Not expected to be material" is the Seller's opinion, not a fact.

**Push back:**
- Pre-Completion covenants: complete the investigation, ideally with an independent forensic report; provide it to us; comply with OAIC and individual notification obligations; consult us on communications.
- Add a **specific indemnity** for all Loss arising from the incident: regulatory investigation costs, notification and remediation, customer claims and credits, and third-party claims. Fines and penalties should be covered to the extent lawfully indemnifiable. The indemnity should sit outside the cap and basket, with survival of at least 3–4 years.
- Strengthen the privacy and data security warranties, and ensure the incident is not "disclosed away."
- Ask whether any customer has been notified or has complained.

### 3.10 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008, DD-011), AUD 330k

**Facts:** There are **three related** renewals of AUD 110k each, which the Disclosure Letter says should be "read together for timing/scope." It does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Why it hurts us:** Splitting one commitment into three equal parts may keep each below a materiality, approval or conduct-of-business threshold in the SPA or the Company's delegations. "Related" also needs explaining: related to each other, or to the Seller? I am not concluding there is any impropriety, but the pattern needs explanation.

**Push back:**
- Obtain DD-008 and DD-011. Confirm the term, termination rights, any prepayments, and whether the supplier is a Seller affiliate.
- Under the conduct-of-business covenants, aggregate related contracts when testing thresholds, and require Buyer consent for new or renewed commitments above an agreed level.
- If the renewals are not genuinely ordinary course, or have been accrued but not paid, treat them as Debt, terminate them pre-Completion at the Seller's cost, or cover them by indemnity.
- If the supplier is a related party, add a warranty on arm's-length terms.

### 3.11 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)

The Seller says neither requires consent for a share sale. That may well be right, but we should verify it ourselves. Change-of-control definitions in leases often capture share sales.

**Push back:**
- Our counsel should review both documents.
- Make delivery of the lease notification a Completion deliverable.
- Add a warranty that no consents or notices are required for the transaction other than those listed in a schedule.

### 3.12 Title (DD-012) and fundamental warranties

**Seller position:** Title is "evidenced by the share register." Fundamentals are to have the same cap and time limit as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."

**Push back:**
- **Reject** the request on fundamentals. Title, capacity, authority, solvency and capitalisation warranties should be capped at 100% of price, survive 6–7 years, and be excluded from disclosure and knowledge qualifications. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap the warranty that says we actually receive the shares.
- Diligence: ASIC company extract and share structure, PPSR search against Harbourglass for security over the shares (see the Riverlark point), constitution and pre-emption waivers, and any options, convertible notes or SAFEs. Harbourglass is a VC vehicle, so check its constituent documents and internal approvals as well.
- Completion deliverables: share certificates (or indemnity for lost certificates), signed transfers, releases of any share security, and director and officer resignations as required.

### 3.13 Tax and IP warranties

"Settled under the general regime" is not accepted. We need:

- a full **tax indemnity** for pre-Completion tax, with ATO-linked survival and a cap at price;
- tax warranties covering R&D incentive claims (if any), payroll tax, GST and employee/contractor characterisation;
- IP warranties covering ownership, Ironquay and contractor assignments, open-source use and no infringement.

### 3.14 Security for claims

Harbourglass Ventures is a fund vehicle that may distribute proceeds soon after Completion. Without security, our warranty and indemnity rights could be worth little.

**Push back:** Propose an **escrow or retention** of around 10–15% of price for 18–24 months, with separate specific retentions for Ironquay and the data incident. Alternatively, consider **W&I insurance** for the general warranties. If we go that route, note that W&I policies exclude known matters, which reinforces the need for specific indemnities and escrow on items 3.5–3.10.

## 4. Summary of recommendations (in priority order)

1. **Reject the "[STANDARD]/FINAL" framing** in writing. All clauses are open. Check with our principals what, if anything, was actually agreed.
2. **Bluefen (~30% of revenue):** hard CP for an unconditional consent (or one on terms acceptable to the Buyer), with cl 11.3 conditions evidenced; Buyer-only waiver; walk right. Otherwise a price adjustment or escrow.
3. **Riverlark (AUD 3.2m):** repay from the funds flow at Completion as Debt; payoff letter before Completion; releases and PPSR discharges *at* Completion; check for security over the shares.
4. **Disclosure and knowledge:** specific, fair disclosure only; delete general data room and public-record disclosure; delete cl 8.3, replacing it with a clause preserving our rights regardless of investigation.
5. **Limitations:** apply to general warranties only. Fraud carve-out. Fundamentals and tax at 100% of price with long survival. Tipping basket. Indemnities outside cap and basket.
6. **Bonuses (AUD 420k plus on-costs):** deduct from price as Transaction Costs and pay through payroll at Completion, with a tax and on-cost indemnity.
7. **Ironquay:** payment evidence and confirmatory IP assignment before Completion, or retention plus a broad IP title indemnity.
8. **DD-006 incident:** obtain an urgent status update on the NDB assessment (the 30-day window has likely run); pre-Completion covenants; specific uncapped-basket indemnity with long survival.
9. **Sandbar (AUD 330k):** explain and document; aggregate for conduct-of-business thresholds; treat as Debt or indemnify if not ordinary course; check for related-party status.
10. **Title:** independent verification (ASIC, PPSR, options and notes); fundamental warranty protection.
11. **Lease and Mossvale:** our own review of the consent position; notices as Completion deliverables.
12. **Security:** escrow or retention (or W&I insurance plus specific retentions for known matters), given the Seller is a fund vehicle.
13. **Updated information:** the data room is stale (cut-off 22 September 2026). Request a bring-down and updates on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and DD-006, on terms that new disclosures do not cure breaches.
